source: A Generous Slice, 24 September to 28 November 2019
editorialPolicy: Public-safe first-person excerpts. Travel, weather, landscape, music and the practical reality of the road are retained; intimate health, relationship, money and identifying third-party details remain in the private journal.

1.label: the first morning
1.text: Woke up feeling ready. I stretched, meditated and headed out to begin my adventure on the road. My navigation immediately took me through beautiful farmland and forestry.

1.label: from the plan
1.text: I believed the lessons I would learn on this journey were worth gaining early, so I could carry them through the rest of my life.

2.label: green lagoon
2.text: A quiet, peaceful path ran beside a clear green river. I had imagined motorways; instead I kept finding fields. Storms always pass.

3.label: château-thierry
3.text: I followed the green river for twenty kilometres. A stranger saw me trying a broken village pump and invited me in for water, kindness crossing the language barrier.

3.label: the church
3.text: In Château-Thierry I stopped in a church and felt a brief moment of transcendence. Later I found my rhythm again and kept moving through the wooded paths.

4.label: fear of wolves
4.text: Rain woke me at two in the morning. In the dark every distant animal sounded like wolves; by daylight I was walking again, heading for the first proper bed of the road.

6.label: return to the road
6.text: After a week of hiking I ran two kilometres faster than I had all trip. The deep breathing and the rhythm let something out; suddenly the road felt like mine again.

7.label: precious moments
7.text: The canal left Châlons-en-Champagne between vineyards and orchards. After running in the boiling sun I lay in a field, still and staring into the sky.

8.label: calm mind, raging storm
8.text: A monumental thunderstorm broke over the route into Bar-le-Duc: pouring rain, lightning and a pause beneath the trees before I carried on.

9.label: peace
9.text: In the woods the wind went still and the sun came through. For a moment everything in the air was calm; nature seemed full of these moments when I noticed them.

11.label: towards nancy
11.text: The path to Nancy ran through a national park in hard rain, with the trees rising high overhead. Even in the weather, voicing the day felt good.

13.label: the courtyard band
13.text: A band playing in a courtyard changed the entire mood of the day. I had forgotten how immediate and transporting live music could be.

13.label: the long canal
13.text: The idea for the road was becoming very simple: if I could not run, I would walk; whatever happened, I would keep moving forward.

14.label: witchi tai to
14.text: The day was hard until cliff faces appeared on both sides of the path, blue flies fluttering between them, and I discovered Witchi Tai To. Magical.

15.label: out of saverne
15.text: Back on the canal out of Saverne, heading for the Rhine and the German border. I wanted to connect to the act of moving and stop worrying about the destination.

16.label: the first border
16.text: Fifteen days after stepping out of Paris, I reached the German border on my own two feet. The first chapter ended with the feeling that my limits had moved.

22.label: munich bound
22.text: Nine consecutive days on the road ended with a late burst of energy towards Munich. The first half had dragged; after dark the pace turned into a proper negative split.

25.label: back from munich
25.text: Two days off the road meant aimless wandering, cold baths, a new backpack and the feeling that I was properly prepared for the hard country ahead.

25.label: another day goes by
25.text: My running rhythm was the best it had been all trip. Friendly conversations, sixty kilometres and the Austrian mountains ahead made this the most natural day of the journey so far.

26.label: one of those days
26.text: The rhythm would not arrive. After a logistical mishap and a flat day I stopped twenty kilometres short of Austria, trusting that tomorrow would be better.

27.label: a sacred land
27.text: Austria began with a sharp climb and a small waterfall. Mountains surrounded the road and the border felt less like a line than the opening of a new landscape.

28.label: the predatory wasp
28.text: A cold, crisp morning became glaring sun. I moved slowly enough to take in the country as the route began to rise towards the Ankogel mountains.

29.label: taking tiger mountain
29.text: A whole new terrain of steep mountain paths opened beneath me. Each climb brought another view across Austria; a large bird circled through the valley below.

30.label: oh how we climbed
30.text: At 2,500 metres it was almost silent: only my breath and footsteps. Streams, scrambles and narrow ridges led over the Tauern, then down empty ski slopes before dark.

31.label: business as usual
31.text: The sun kept beaming down despite it being almost November. Another fifty kilometres had begun to feel methodical, the body adapting to what once felt enormous.

32.label: the new normal
32.text: Lacing my shoes, heading for the trails and covering forty kilometres had become ordinary everyday life. I had to step back to remember it was unusual at all.

33.label: katy song
33.text: Living on the bare minimum clarified what was missing: human interaction. Even a short conversation at the end of the day changed my energy completely.

34.label: sing me to sleep
34.text: The previous day had wound through odd little scenes: goats on roofs, scarecrows appearing more often than people, and quiet roads between them.

35.label: the process
35.text: I stopped tracking every kilometre so closely. The point was to fall in love with the process and notice the day-to-day details instead of planning the future.

36.label: beyond me, beyond you
36.text: More than fifty kilometres through drizzle, wind chill, waterlogged paths and fog ended with one final steep wooded climb in darkness.

37.label: skipper
37.text: Another fifty kilometres in rain and low temperatures. Slovenia had been brief and hard; arriving in Ptuj to a warm welcome changed the evening.

38.label: entering croatia
38.text: Croatia arrived after nearly fifteen consecutive days on the road: first the main road with cars rushing past, then the welcome quiet of a canal path.

40.label: after the rest day
40.text: Fifteen days without real rest had made six or seven hours of walking feel like a rest day. I slept before making any decision, then returned to the road.

40.label: distant sky
40.text: Grey roads and monotonous trails headed east across Croatia. Osijek became the next clear point on the horizon and the promise of a proper pause.

41.label: biscuit town
41.text: A warm, sunny day crossed the sparse northern Croatian plain. Weeks after the Austrian mountains, the empty land made the scale of everything feel different.

42.label: sweet road
42.text: Trains bridged the unsafe main-road sections. After the last stop, forty kilometres of flat farms stretched ahead in one long, geometric line to Osijek.

47.label: eyes open wide
47.text: New shoes, a half-marathon run and an early finish returned the sense of moving with intention. Beside the Croatian road stood an unexpected warning sign for mines.

48.label: entering serbia
48.text: The last muddy fields of Croatia led to passport control, then river paths, fishermen and small huts on the Serbian side beneath a dark grey sky.

49.label: the furthest day
49.text: Seventy kilometres to Novi Sad: the furthest I had ever travelled on foot. After dark the route became technical paths, bushes and pure determination.

52.label: disorder
52.text: A late start became a race against sunset. The faster I ran, the more mud gathered under my shoes; the final five kilometres were uneven ground in darkness.

53.label: belgrade
53.text: Walking into Belgrade in perfect weather, I decided to take my time before the final push. The day itself was a long, straightforward line into the city.

56.label: leaving belgrade
56.text: Out before seven in crisp weather, I found a new speed. Brambles, a small mountain and the dark all passed without the old anxiety of a fixed destination.

57.label: a plea for tenderness
57.text: A full day of walking on farm tracks, small tractors chugging past. One farmer tipped his hat and waved; the smallest acknowledgement lifted the whole mood.

58.label: i'll come too
58.text: A pipeline construction made an unexpectedly direct path. The guesthouse welcome was tea, wafers and home-brewed raki, with comedy supplied by the language barrier.

59.label: dogmeat
59.text: A very short day with a stray dog for company. I called him Dogmeat and, for part of the road, he simply followed along.

62.label: music for a found harmonium
62.text: I am reborn. My beard is gone; I am ready to carry on forward. Nothing can stop me.

63.label: the two towers
63.text: Near the end, doubt kept returning and some days felt like a chore. But I had never called it a holiday; from the beginning it was a challenge.

64.label: banshee beat
64.text: My purpose was simple: to encourage other people to find what makes them happy and pursue it. The road kept testing whether I could live that idea myself.

65.label: country seven
65.text: Crossing into Bulgaria made the end suddenly real. Sofia was one more day away; the journey I had imagined for months was almost complete.

66.label: sofia
66.text: I arrived in Sofia and planned to sit with the journey for a few days, revisiting the memories and beginning to write the road down while it was still close.
